claims.text: The pattern: give agents that work together an encrypted vault as their shared memory and their way of talking, and let it exist only for as long as the work does.
claims.quote: give them an encrypted vault as their shared memory and their way of talking, and let it exist only for as long as the work does

claims.text: Capture the pattern as a series of architectures from simple to complex, each in a repository of its own with its agents, keys, fixtures and a CI job that proves it works, forkable as templates, recipes and skills.
claims.quote: each in a repository of its own with its agents, its keys, its fixtures and a CI job that proves it works

claims.text: The repository should run as one of the checks before anything reaches sgit's main branch.
claims.quote: The repository should run as one of the checks before anything reaches sgit's main branch.

claims.text: Every architecture answers four questions, memory, communication, asynchrony and visibility, and the answer depends on who holds which key.
claims.quote: The answer depends on who holds which key.

claims.text: Because the only thing that leaves the environment is ciphertext, logs and data can be stored where you would not normally trust them; it is all about the decryption keys and whether the vault is ephemeral.
claims.quote: Because the only thing that ever leaves the environment is ciphertext

claims.text: Most agents on this site already work this way: the wire agent reads vaults research desks write holding only the read key, isolated agents keep memory in a vault, and a vault is the shared file system, channel and record.
claims.quote: a vault is the shared file system, the message channel and the record, and its keys decide who can do what

claims.text: Many of these vaults are ephemeral: when the work is done they can be deleted from the server or left as ciphertext nobody holds the key to.
claims.quote: or simply left as ciphertext nobody holds the key to

claims.text: The seven architectures run from one agent with one ephemeral vault, through writer and readers, fan-out by folder, append-only workers, no network, and watched, to a swarm of a hundred; a scoped clone is a speed setting, the boundary is the key.
claims.quote: a scoped clone is a speed setting, not a boundary: the boundary is the key

claims.text: In the no-network architecture sgit reads a vault from a folder read-only with its local transport, and a courier outside the sandbox moves the encrypted files in and out and holds no keys at all.
claims.quote: a courier outside the sandbox moves the encrypted files in and out and holds no keys at all

claims.text: Each architecture should be shown in three environments, and since Claude Code can run background subagents concurrently, a single session can exercise them rather than a fleet.
claims.quote: Background subagents run concurrently while you continue working.

claims.text: A vault app gives the visual representation people ask for: a page that lives in the vault draws its contents, a screenshot is stored back in the vault, and the vault's key stays in the host.
claims.quote: open the vault, the app draws its contents, take a screenshot, store it in the vault, and carry on

claims.text: A vault server runs as a Docker image and sgit can serve a vault's published folder locally, so the viewer can run wherever the agents do.
claims.quote: A vault server runs as a Docker image

claims.text: With in-memory storage, a hundred writers posting ten entries each landed all 1,000 entries in an append lane in 4.9 seconds, about 205 a second, and every accepted entry was listed afterwards.
claims.quote: A hundred writers posting ten entries each landed all 1,000 in 4.9 seconds, about 205 a second.

value.unit: entries landed in 4.9 seconds by a hundred writers

claims.text: Measured with sgit 0.21.0 and vault server 0.34.0 as one process on four cores, 1, 10, 50 and 100 writers each posting one 2 KB entry took 0.004, 0.03, 0.12 and 0.27 seconds.
claims.quote: took 0.004, 0.03, 0.12 and 0.27 seconds

value.unit: seconds for 100 writers posting one entry each

claims.text: A hundred writers sharing one token sent 1,200 entries; exactly 1,000 were accepted and 200 refused at the server's cap of 1,000 waiting entries per inbox, the case for one token per worker.
claims.quote: exactly 1,000 were accepted and 200 refused at the server's cap of 1,000 waiting entries per inbox

value.unit: entries refused at the inbox cap

claims.text: Ten scoped clones of one folder of a 2,000-file vault at once took 1.9 seconds with the server mostly idle; ten full clones of a 500-file vault took 21.1, on one core of a single process.
claims.quote: Ten full clones of a 500-file vault took 21.1

value.unit: seconds for ten full clones, against 1.9 for ten scoped clones

claims.text: A scoped clone barely grows with the vault, 0.59 seconds at 100 files and 0.77 at 2,000, while a full clone went from 0.95 to 5.55.
claims.quote: 0.59 seconds at 100 files, 0.77 at 2,000, while a full clone went from 0.95 to 5.55

value.unit: seconds for a scoped clone at 2,000 files

claims.text: The same run found four defects no demo would show: disk storage scans the whole store on every append, files over 4 MB fail on local disk, a headless clone could not fetch one file, and full clones queue on one process.
claims.quote: The same run found four problems, none of which a demo would have shown

claims.text: That is the argument for the repository as a release gate: the architectures get complex fast and exercise exactly the features that change between releases.
claims.quote: That is the argument for the repository as a release gate.

claims.text: The brief in eight items: a folder per architecture, a CI job each, three environments, a vault app each, the swarm test as a repeatable job, the defects as issues, the gate before sgit's main branch, and templates.
claims.quote: The repository runs before a release reaches sgit's main branch; a failure blocks it.

claims.text: What to be careful about: no key in a repository, a log or a screenshot; ephemeral means deleted, each run cleans up its vaults; and the swarm test is for a server we run.
claims.quote: Ephemeral means deleted: each run cleans up its vaults.

claims.text: The numbers are local: one four-core machine and one server process, and the append-lane and concurrency rows ran once.
claims.quote: One four-core machine and one server process; the append-lane and concurrency rows ran once.

claims.text: The disk numbers show a defect, not the design; the in-memory figures are closer to it and slow down as the store grows.
claims.quote: The disk numbers show a defect, not the design.

claims.text: Architectures 5, 6 and 7 are proposed; 2 and 4 build on what the site runs, and the rest are untested here.
claims.quote: 2 and 4 build on what this site runs; the rest are untested here.

claims.text: Nothing in the brief is built.
claims.quote: Nothing in the brief is built.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 14 October 2026 written by the site's writer agent; the measurements were run by a research agent on one machine against a local vault server with throwaway vaults.
claims.quote: The measurements were run for this article by a research agent on one machine
